the cuticle of the dorsal carapaces of the edible crab, Cancer pagurus, is a highly heterogeneous material with respect to chemical composition and mechanical properties, which are correlated to structural organization.
the exoskeleton of Cancer pagurus exhibits a complex structural hierarchy with a heterogeneous mineralization, resulting in a heterogeneous mechanical response of the material.

the cuticle of the dorsal carapaces of Cancer pagurus is a complex composite material with different structural levels and mineral phases, which show a high degree of heterogeneity in structure and composition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a detailed characterization of the structural organization and mechanical behaviour of the exoskeletal cuticle of a crustacean.
the correlation of structural organization, composition and local properties of the cuticle from the carapace of C. pagurus.
the structural and mechanical characterization of the exoskeletal material of a marine crustacean and the correlation of structure, chemical composition and mechanical properties.

the cuticle in the dorsal carpace of Cancer pagurus is a complex material with a hierarchical structure and composition, which is optimized for the function of this skeletal element.
the hierarchical organization of structure and composition in the cuticle of crustaceans has a strong influence on its mechanical behaviour.
the hierarchical organization of the cuticle is a result of a compromise between mechanical requirements, environmental conditions and metabolic costs.

the hierarchical structure of cuticle is reflected in the chemical composition and mechanical properties on the local level.
the cuticle is a highly heterogeneous material with respect to structure, composition and mechanical properties, and this heterogeneity is the basis of the functionality of this material.
the exoskeleton of the crab Cancer pagurus is highly optimized in its structural hierarchy, chemical composition and mechanical properties to fulfill the different functions in the carapace.

the hierarchical structure of the crustacean exoskeleton, in combination with its heterogeneous chemical composition, is a key factor to understand the complex mechanical properties of the exoskeletal cuticle.
the local structural organization of cuticle is highly heterogeneous and that this heterogeneity is reflected in the local mechanical properties.
